sentences.text: This section defines how apron movement management is executed after the Airport Duty Manager handover has identified active surface constraints.
In ramp operations, Ramp Control Lead is also called Quartzline during voice and chat coordination.
The Ramp Control Lead maintains the operational sequence for pushbacks, stand exits, stand entries, and towing movements within the controlled apron area.

Pushback sequencing is based on safety separation, published stand constraints, crew readiness, ground handling completion, and the relationship between Target Off Block Time and Calculated Takeoff Time.
The Ramp Control Lead shall not release a pushback until the Tower Supervisor has confirmed that the movement can be integrated with the active ground route and runway plan.
The Ramp Movement Board is the primary working view for planned apron movements, active conflicts, towing tasks, and occupied stand intervals.
Surface Surveillance Adapter inputs support the Ramp Control Lead by confirming aircraft position, stand occupancy, and blocking conditions on critical apron lanes.
East Apron Sensor and West Apron Sensor indications are used as supporting evidence, but the Ramp Control Lead remains responsible for reconciling sensor data with visual and operational reports.

The Ramp Control Lead assigns priority to towing movements that remove a blocking aircraft, protect a confirmed departure sequence, or create capacity for an inbound aircraft with no equivalent stand option.
Routine maintenance tows are normally sequenced behind live departure and arrival movements unless an operational safety issue requires earlier action.
Ramp Control Lead sends the Stand Tow Request Form when a parked aircraft must be repositioned to release a stand, remove an apron blockage, or support a confirmed operating plan.
Apron occupancy is managed as a time-based resource, with each stand treated as unavailable from the start of servicing until the aircraft and equipment are clear of the marked safety area.
The Gate Conflict Detector alerts the Ramp Control Lead when a planned arrival, departure, or tow would create an overlapping occupancy condition at a stand or adjacent service lane.

When a conflict is detected, the Ramp Control Lead coordinates with the Ground Handling Dispatcher to confirm whether servicing progress, equipment availability, or staffing constraints can change the sequence.
The Handling Resource Planner provides the shared planning basis for baggage, catering, cleaning, boarding support, and towing resources that affect apron readiness.
The Ramp Control Lead reviews Handling Resource Planner constraints before committing to a pushback sequence that depends on rapid equipment removal or immediate stand reuse.
Airline Operations Coordinator participation is required when a resequence would materially affect passenger boarding, connection protection, or aircraft rotation plans.
The Aircraft Operator Representative remains accountable for operator acceptance of any revised off-block expectation that results from ramp resequencing.
Marlinstone shall refresh stand demand forecasts when the Ramp Movement Board records a material change in planned off-block timing.
The Tower Sequence Manager receives the current ramp intent through system synchronization so that apron releases and runway metering remain consistent.
If apron congestion begins to affect runway delivery, the Ramp Control Lead escalates the condition to the Tower Supervisor and Airport Duty Manager for a coordinated mitigation decision.
During Adverse Weather Mode, the Ramp Control Lead increases spacing between pushbacks and towing movements to account for slower ground servicing and reduced driver visibility.
During Capacity Reduction State, apron movements are prioritized to prevent stand saturation and to preserve access for emergency routes and critical service lanes.
All material resequencing decisions are recorded in the Collaborative Decision Log with the reason, affected aircraft, coordinating parties, and time of approval.
The Audit Event Ledger retains movement updates from the Ramp Movement Board so that post-event review can compare planned sequencing with actual apron performance.
